I want to give a heartfelt thank you to the entire China Grove team and Dr. Robin for showing Daisy and me so much care, compassion, and kindness during one of the hardest moments I have ever had to face.
Daisy was 16 years old and lived a long, fulfilled life. She was the leader of our pack and such a special girl who brought so much love and meaning to our life. She enjoyed her days basking in the sun, patrolling her territory, chewing on soccer balls, playing in the water, eating all the leftovers, and simply enjoying the little things. I will always be grateful for all the years, memories, and love she gave me.
When Daisy’s health rapidly declined and she was suffering, everyone went above and beyond to squeeze her in at the last moment and make sure she was comfortable. The entire team was so compassionate and understanding from the moment I walked through the door. They took the time to explain everything to me step by step and made sure I wasn’t scared or unsure of what was happening. They walked me through the entire process, answered all of my questions, and made such a heartbreaking experience a little easier to get through.
This was the first time I have ever had to put a pet down, let alone my childhood dog, so it was an incredibly difficult experience for me. Saying goodbye to Daisy was one of the hardest things I have ever had to do, but I am so grateful that she was surrounded by such caring people who treated her with so much love, gentleness, and dignity during her final moments.
Thank you so much to the entire China Grove team — every vet, vet tech, staff member, and doctor who cared for Daisy and helped me through that day. I have been bringing all of my pets and my family’s pets to this team for years, and the care has always been over the top. It truly shows how much you care for each animal and every family that walks through your doors.
It’s never easy saying goodbye, but I am so grateful Daisy was able to live such a long and happy, life. She was loved deeply throughout her 16 years, and she will be missed more than words can say.
Thank you for taking such good care of my girl when I needed you most. I will forever be grateful for the compassion and kindness you showed Daisy and me.

Went in today; my dog tested positive for parvo. They suggested all kinds of things and said there was a good chance he'd make it, that these treatments were the best. I agreed to their suggestions. As they were injecting him, his head was weak and body limp; his temperature had dropped more. They still went ahead and injected him. As we were backing out, I asked my husband to stop because my dog was dead. I walked back in with my dog in my arms, and the veterinarian said he still had a heartbeat, yet his head and body were limp. I said my dog was dying. She asked if I wanted to euthanize him. I said, "You just charged me $836.88 for a treatment that you said works very well, and my dog is dying." I walked out, and my dog died in my arms not more than 10 minutes later. I called and asked for a partial refund, and I was told that the manager would get back to me. If they would have said, "Look at him, he looks like he might not make it," I would have thought of euthanization and not had my dog and us suffer seeing him die in my arms. But the truth is, they only cared about the money, on selling food, IV fluid, nausea injections, and a vaccine that alone cost $440.00.
